title: Infinity Proposal v1
description: What a caller asks the kernel to judge. The kernel itself is more lenient than this contract: it ignores unknown fields, accepts any JSON payload, and answers a wrong version, an unknown effect or an unknown risk with a logged `deny` rather than a parse error. This contract describes what a well-formed producer sends; a proposal that fails it is still safe to submit, and is expected to be denied.

actor.description: Who is asking, as the caller says. It is recorded and hashed, so it cannot be changed afterwards without breaking the log, but the kernel never reads it and no policy rule can use it. It is not authenticated: it is as trustworthy as the process that wrote it. Do not read it as proof of who acted.

effect.description: The kernel knows read, write, deploy, authority_change and audit_delete. Anything else is denied as UNKNOWN_EFFECT; deploy, authority_change and audit_delete are always denied as FORBIDDEN_EFFECT.

risk.description: The kernel knows low, medium, high and critical. Anything else is denied as UNKNOWN_RISK.

policy_version.description: Must equal the policy's policy_id, or the proposal is denied as POLICY_MISMATCH.

payload.description: Free-form facts about the request. Never the content itself (Nova sends sizes and a hash). A `verdict` key is refused by the kernel: a proposal cannot choose its own verdict.

evidence_refs.description: References to evidence for the request.

approval_id.description: Set only when re-submitting a request a human approved. Not part of the hash a human approval is bound to.

call_digest.description: SHA-256 of a concrete call, sha256:<64 lowercase hex>. Optional. The kernel hashes it and does not interpret it. The signer fills it when the request includes a call; a proposal that only states it is the caller's claim.
